messages:
paul.r: Quick sync — GreenLeaf SI ran integration smoke last night and hit three surprises: (1) their runtime failed image signature verification when pulling our marketplace artifact, (2) Ansible playbook errors during post-deploy config (permissions on /etc/redwood), and (3) CUDA driver mismatch on their GPU nodes causing the model server to crash. They flagged a potential joint announcement timeline risk.

nina.l: Oof. Do we have the image signature policy documented for SIs? They might be verifying a signing key we rotated last month.

paul.r: Exactly. Error they reported: `containerd: failed to verify image signature: signature verification failed: public key not found: rsa-key-2025-03` — they copied the key id.

jordan.m: That key id matches the old signing key we rotated to `rsa-key-2025-08`. Looks like their allowlist still references the deprecated key. Two options: give GreenLeaf the new key and a short migration instruction, or re-sign the image with the old key (not great for security). Recommend send the new key and a small checklist.

reliability-bot: Note: signing-key deprecation policy requires re-signing only under exceptional ops approval. Fresh signatures must use active keys.

nina.l: Agreed, no re-sign. @paul.r can you push the new public key and a verification snippet to the SI? Eg: ```bash
# fetch public signing key
curl -sS https://artifacts.redwood.ai/keys/rsa-key-2025-08.pub -o redwood.pub
# verify image
cosign verify --key redwood.pub ghcr.io/redwood/private-runtime:v3.0.1
```

paul.r: Will do. Next, Ansible errors — they posted this: `fatal: [edge-node]: FAILED! => {"msg": "file could not be written: permission denied"}` during templating `/etc/redwood/config.yaml`. They run the playbook as non-root via systemd.

jordan.m: We added a fallback that writes config to `/var/lib/redwood` if `/etc/redwood` is not writable. Maybe their playbook template didn't pick that up. Ask them to run `ansible-playbook site.yml -e redwood_config_path=/var/lib/redwood` as a temporary workaround.

paul.r: I'll share that. Also will push a small patch to the Ansible role to ensure directories are created with proper permissions when using non-root deploys.

security: For the signing key, include the fingerprint and verification steps in the handoff doc. Also note we rotate keys quarterly; remind SIs to fetch keys via our signed key endpoint rather than hardcoding. I'll approve the wording.

paul.r: Last: CUDA driver mismatch. Their nodes are on `nvidia-driver 515.86` but our optimized Triton build expects `>= 530`. Crash log: `CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version`.

jordan.m: We should provide two paths: (A) recommend they upgrade drivers to 530+ (best), or (B) use our CPU-optimized model bundle temporarily. If they choose upgrade we can provide a quick driver compatibility checklist and a maintenance window slot.

nina.l: They want the announcement in two weeks. If drivers aren't upgraded, it's risky to promise performance numbers. Let's make the joint announcement contingent on driver compatibility sign-off.

paul.r: Proposed action list: (1) send public key and verification snippet (owner: paul) (2) Ansible role patch + one-line workaround (owner: jordan) (3) driver compatibility note + offered maintenance window (owner: jordan) (4) update partnership-runbook with signing key rotation guidance and non-root Ansible steps (owner: nina) (5) security to vet the public key distribution wording (owner: security).

jordan.m: I'll open PR for Ansible role and draft the driver note. If GreenLeaf needs temporary CPU bundle, I can stage it in their tenant.

paul.r: Scheduling a remediation call today 16:00 UTC with GreenLeaf ops. Sharing calendar now. We should include one SI engineer, one infra eng, and security on the call.

reliability-bot: Reminder: any temporary artifact distribution must be logged. Enable artifact-access audit for tenant `greenleaf-prod` during the window.

nina.l: Thanks. Also I'll flag the announcement plan: marketing should get a holdback until ops confirms GPU validation. I'll add a checkpoint to the go/no-go checklist.

security: Approved the key distribution blurb; please don't include private keys in invites.

paul.r: All set. I'll post the key link and the Ansible workaround in the remediation invite and follow up here after the call. :rocket:
